strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Uses 8 sequential all-reduce operations (one per dependent iteration) with local compute between each. Each iteration computes block means, scales by f[b], performs all-reduce, then unscales. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches with full 2048-element payload each time. Represents the straightforward implementation with no fusion or pipelining.

strategies.name: Fused Pre-Compute with Vectorized Scaling
strategies.desc: Performs initial all-reduce to get summed vector, then fuses all 8 dependent iterations by vectorizing the scale/unscale operations and block mean computations to minimize intermediate buffer allocations. Still requires 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead by batching tensor operations and eliminating redundant clones. Trades implementation complexity for reduced memory traffic.

strategies.name: Block-Parallel Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather
strategies.desc: Decomposes each iteration into reduce-scatter (distributing 8 blocks across subset of ranks) followed by local compute on assigned blocks, then all-gather to reassemble. For 224 ranks, can partition into groups where each processes fewer blocks. Increases total collective count (16 dispatches: 8 RS + 8 AG) but reduces per-dispatch payload size and enables parallel block processing.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node topology by splitting the 8 iterations into intra-node and inter-node phases. Performs local reductions within nodes first (smaller world size, faster latency), then cross-node reductions. With num_nodes parameter, can optimize for network topology. Total dispatches remain 8 all-reduces but with hierarchical collective implementation reducing cross-node bandwidth.

strategies.name: Overlapped Compute-Communication Pipeline
strategies.desc:
Splits the 2048-element vector into independent chunks and pipelines different iteration stages across chunks using async collectives. While iteration i+1's all-reduce is in flight for chunk A, compute block means and scaling for iteration i on chunk B. Requires careful dependency management but can hide communication latency behind computation. Dispatch count varies (8-16) depending on chunk granularity.
